coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:2231-2244 drains coordinator events during checkpoint and marks Ready.
coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:2177-2183 consumes control interactions only after checkpoint_with_realtime returns.
coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/process.rs:1758-1769 admits interactions regardless of lifecycle permit or coordinator readiness.
findings.impact: If a checkpoint overlaps the server readiness transition, an interaction emitted before Ready can remain queued throughout the checkpoint and then be forwarded as though it were post-Ready, violating the sealed drop-before-Ready boundary.
findings.observation: Checkpoint draining advances the coordinator's Ready state without concurrently consuming or timestamping the control interaction FIFO, so queued interactions can cross the readiness cutover.
findings.recommendation: Make the Ready cutover and interaction classification explicit across checkpoints: drain and drop every interaction known to precede Ready while checkpoint correlation remains live, then begin forwarding only interactions admitted after the cutover, preserving FIFO. Add a deterministic before/after Ready regression.

findings.impact: A peer-controlled lifecycle flood can continue driving ROM lifecycle state after the realtime core has already classified the attempt as terminal.
findings.observation: RealtimeCoordinator::next_event polls owner.recv_event before the realtime JoinHandle, so a completed OwnerBackpressure task can coexist with queued lifecycle events that are forwarded first.
findings.recommendation: Give task completion priority over owner events, discard queued owner events once terminal, and add a saturated-owner-queue regression proving no lifecycle forwarding after OwnerBackpressure.
